difficultyReason: Chronology is subtle: bones above the lava + lake lasted 500,000 years → ancestors lived at that time, BUT only if the bones entered the sediments while the lake was forming, not after it dried. Necessary-assumption negation test is sharp.
stimulus: About two million years ago, lava dammed up a river in western Asia and caused a small lake to form. The lake existed for about half a million years. Bones of an early human ancestor were recently found in the ancient lake-bottom sediments that lie on top of the layer of lava. Therefore, ancestors of modern humans lived in western Asia between two million and one-and-a-half million years ago.
questionStem: Which one of the following is an assumption required by the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There were no other lakes in the immediate area before the lava dammed up the river.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The lake contained fish that the human ancestors could have used for food.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lava that lay under the lake-bottom sediments did not contain any human fossil remains.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lake was deep enough that a person could drown in it.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bones were already in the sediments by the time the lake dried up.

explanations.correct: Negate E: the bones were NOT in the sediments by the time the lake dried up — i.e., they arrived later. Then the bones don't date the humans to the 2-1.5 Mya window. The conclusion collapses, so E is necessary.
explanations.A: Other lakes are irrelevant to dating the bones in this one.
explanations.B: Fish are not required for human presence.
explanations.C: The argument is about what's above the lava, not within it.
explanations.D: Drowning is not the causal mechanism invoked.

source.notes: Verbatim from LSAC public LR sample page. Correct answer E confirmed.
